styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Deira, the creek abras and the Al Fahidi lanes.

styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Jumeirah sand, Marina promenade and desert sunsets.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Gold souk haggling to the Dubai Mall.

stays.why: Walk to Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall; Metro Red Line on the doorstep.
Beach and promenade at the door; Metro and tram nearby for the rest of the city.
Cheapest beds, gold and spice souks, creek abras; Metro Green Line links Downtown.
Beach hotels and quiet streets; taxis needed for most sights.

food: Try Emirati dishes: machboos rice, harees and luqaimat dumplings with date syrup.
Cheap eats in Deira and Bur Dubai: shawarma, karak tea and Indian cafeterias, roughly AED 10–30 a meal.
Fish and grills along Jumeirah Beach Road; book ahead for weekend brunch in hotels.
Alcohol is served only in licensed hotel bars and restaurants. Dress modestly in souks and malls.
During Ramadan, daytime eating is restricted in public; many hotels serve iftar buffets in the evening.
more_time: Swap a mall afternoon for a desert safari: dune drive and dinner, roughly AED 150–350, book a licensed operator.
Take an abra across the creek (AED 1–2) and wander the Al Fahidi historic lanes and the souks.
Add a day trip to Abu Dhabi or Hatta; check bus and tour prices on the day.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the souks, a beach day and the Burj Khalifa without rushing, and leaves room for a desert evening.

month_notes: January: mild days around 24°C, cool nights; best month for walking the souks.
February: similar to January, a couple of rain days; pack a light layer.
March: warming to 28°C; good beach weather before the heat builds.
April: 33°C by day; do outdoor sights in the morning.
May: 37°C and dry; move to malls, museums and evening plans.
June: 40°C; stay indoors midday, hydrate constantly.
July: hottest month, 41°C highs and 31°C nights; plan around air-conditioning.
August: as hot as July; beaches only at sunrise or after sunset.
September: still 39°C; indoor sights and evening creek walks.
October: cooling to 35°C; outdoor days become pleasant again.
November: 31°C and dry; excellent for beach and desert trips.
December: mild 26°C days, cool evenings; busy holiday season, book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: sunny nearly every day, very little rain, and a long, humid summer.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 24–31°C with cool evenings. Ideal for beaches, souks and the desert.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 39–41°C with humid nights near 30°C. Go outside only early or after dark.

items.title: Humid by the coast
items.text: Muggy evenings from May to October; expect fogged sunglasses leaving air-conditioning.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: Only 0–2 rain days a month, mostly December to March. No umbrella needed most of the year.

items.title: Occasional dust
items.text: Spring and early summer can bring hazy, dusty skies; desert trips may be cancelled.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, hat and strong sunscreen; a light layer for winter nights and cold AC; modest wear for souks and mosques.

transit.best: Metro for Downtown and Marina; taxis or ride apps for everything else.

modes.text: Red and Green lines link the airport, Downtown and Marina; fares AED 3–7.50 with a Silver nol card.
Buses cover the rest of the city; tap out at the end of every ride.
Easy to flag; Careem and Uber both work in Dubai.
Driving is common; rent a car with an International Driving Permit.
Fine in Marina and Deira but hard in summer heat; abras cross the creek for AED 1–2.
Small wooden boats cross the creek for AED 1–2; the cheapest ride in the city.
